held.why: REFUSED: False claim: "cheetah and race come from racing". A cheetah is an animal, not something that comes from racing.
REFUSED: False claim: "towel and puddle are simply wet things". A towel is a thing for drying, not a wet thing; "simply" is also the banned word's family.

REFUSED: Fault in the question as well as the script: FAIR is a three-sense headword the vr04 machinery retires from bare cards (register R1045/R1047 hold: which sense does the card carry?), and the key "just" is itself read by a child as "only". The gloss "even, square and right" also leans on the idiom "fair and square" a 9-11-year-old may not know.
REFUSED: Untrue claims: "It means bare and quite unfilled" (hollow does not mean bare) and "log and drum are hollow things" (a log is normally solid).
REFUSED: Wrong strength: "This word means fairly uncommon." Rare means not found often, not fairly uncommon; in a family whose distractors test strength, the gloss teaches the wrong one.
REFUSED: Names a word not on the screen: "Dutiful carries that meaning too." The options are well-behaved, disobedient, dog and command; the key well-behaved is never named.
REFUSED: Untrue and unclear gloss: "It describes strong and pouring light." Luminous means giving off light, often a soft glow; "pouring light" is not a phrase a child can use.
REFUSED: Not readable English for a 9-11-year-old: "It stands for widely bad fame." The gloss does not parse, so the step to infamous is not shown.
